title: Outcomes and complications of parathyroidectomy in otorhinolaryngology practice: A single-institution, 10-year retrospective observational study.
abstract: Background Parathyroidectomy is associated with a spectrum of potential complications, including recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) injury, permanent hypocalcemia, postoperative hemorrhage, wound infection, and recurrence of hyperparathyroidism (HPT). The objective of this study was to evaluate the outcomes of 223 parathyroid procedures and to determine the incidence of procedure-related complications. Methods This retrospective observational study analyzed parathyroidectomy cases performed between 2013 and 2022. Demographic data and postoperative complications were collected and assessed. The success rates of surgical removal of parathyroid adenomas, hyperplasia, carcinomas, and cysts were evaluated in relation to preoperative and perioperative diagnostic methods. Results A total of 223 parathyroidectomy procedures were performed. Unilateral permanent RLN palsy was observed in 0.91% of cases (95% CI, 0.11-3.21%). Bilateral permanent vocal cord palsy was not observed. A positive response to the parathyroidectomy was observed in 98.43% (95% CI, 96.1-99.72%). Temporary hypercalcemia developed in 13.26% (95% CI, 9.41-18.35%). Revision surgery for persistent HPT or recurrence of HPT was necessary in 16 cases. Conclusion The combination of preoperative multimodal imaging and precise hyperparathyroidism diagnosis is essential for reducing the risk of unsuccessful localization in parathyroid surgery. Ultrasound and scintigraphy offers the most effective diagnostic method. Intraoperative neuromonitoring is recommended for revision surgeries.

title: Expert assessment of medical and organizational care for children with congenital ear malformations in the Republic of Kazakhstan: The RAND/UCLA appropriateness method.
abstract: Congenital auditory anomalies are serious conditions ranging from mild hearing loss to complete deafness, with associated speech impairment, social limitations, and disability. Our aim was to evaluate the appropriateness of medical and organizational care interventions for children with congenital ear malformations (microtia and aural atresia) in the Republic of Kazakhstan, using the RAND/UCLA Appropriateness Method. Methods A nine-member multidisciplinary expert panel (otorhinolaryngologists, audiologists, pediatricians, and otologic surgeons) rated 93 diagnostic, therapeutic, and rehabilitation interventions using a structured 9-point appropriateness scale across two rounds of evaluation. Consensus was defined as a numerical IQR (Q3-Q1) ≤2 score points combined with ≥75% of ratings within the same category. Appropriateness categories were defined as: Appropriate (median 7-9), Uncertain (4-6), and Inappropriate (1-3). Results Of 93 rated interventions, 43 (46%) reached consensus as Appropriate, 45 (48%) were classified as Uncertain, and 5 (5%) as Inappropriate. Highest appropriateness was assigned to multidisciplinary diagnostic consultations (ENT specialist, audiologist, otologic surgeon) and imaging (high-resolution CT of the temporal bones, MRI). For bilateral aural atresia, bone conduction devices were rated as Appropriate (mean 7.55-7.66). Non-intervention approaches received the lowest ratings (mean 1.11-3.00), indicating strong expert consensus against expectant management. Key organizational barriers were included as explicitly rated items in the questionnaire (items 85-93, Section 4-5 of Appendix A). Delayed or absent patient registration and follow-up (item 86, mean 8.00, median 8, Appropriate) and inadequacies in regulatory frameworks (item 87, mean 7.22, median 7, Appropriate†) were among the highest-rated organizational items, while insufficient funding (item 88, mean 6.22, median 6, Uncertain without consensus) did not reach consensus. Conclusion This first application of the RAND/UCLA method in Kazakhstan to evaluate care for children with congenital ear malformations identified clear areas of expert consensus and uncertainty. The results support the development of multidisciplinary care pathways and targeted rehabilitation policies. Findings represent structured expert opinion from nine specialist panelists in Kazakhstan and should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, or national representativeness.

title: Capivasertib plus abiraterone in PTEN-deficient de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer: updated survival analysis from CAPItello-281.
abstract: Background Patients with phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN)-deficient de novo metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (mHSPC) have poor prognosis and reduced benefit from current standard of care. The phase III CAPItello-281 study (NCT04493853) showed a statistically significant benefit in radiographic progression-free survival (rPFS) with capivasertib plus abiraterone versus placebo plus abiraterone (combined with prednisone/prednisolone and androgen deprivation therapy): hazard ratio (HR) 0.81, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.66-0.98; P=0.034. The HR for interim overall survival (OS; 26% maturity) was 0.90, 95% CI 0.71-1.15. Here, we report ad hoc, descriptive analyses at 42% OS data maturity. Patients and methods Patients with de novo mHSPC and PTEN-deficient tumors (defined as ≥90% of viable malignant cells with no specific cytoplasmic staining by immunohistochemistry) received capivasertib plus abiraterone or matched placebo (randomized 1:1) plus abiraterone. Analyses performed at this ad hoc data cut-off, including the alpha-controlled key secondary endpoint of OS as well as the primary endpoint of investigator-assessed rPFS, were descriptive and not prespecified in the protocol. Results 1012 patients received capivasertib plus abiraterone (n=507) or placebo plus abiraterone (n=505). At this ad hoc analysis at 42% OS maturity (data cut-off: March 9, 2026), with 17 months' additional follow-up (median follow-up 39 months in both arms), HR for OS favored capivasertib plus abiraterone versus placebo plus abiraterone (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68-0.99, P=0.044) and OS medians were reached: 57.4 versus 46.5 months. Updated rPFS (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.70-0.99, nominal P=0.033; median 35.5 versus 26.0 months) was consistent with the primary analysis. The safety profile remained consistent with the primary findings. Conclusions With longer follow-up, findings from this updated descriptive analysis support the clinically meaningful OS benefit of adding capivasertib to abiraterone in the treatment of patients with PTEN-deficient mHSPC. Capivasertib plus abiraterone represents a first-in-class targeted treatment approach for this poor prognosis population with high unmet need.

title: [Imaging of pulmonary nodules: A diagnostic approach].
abstract: The detection of pulmonary nodules has increased considerably with the widespread use of chest-computed tomography and the development of low-dose CT lung cancer screening. The pulmonary nodule represents a major diagnostic challenge, requiring rigorous evaluation in order to distinguish benign from malignant lesions while limiting unnecessary invasive investigations. Analysis relies on precise morphological characterization (density, size, margins), assessment of persistence and growth over time, and integration of the clinical context. The Fleischner Society guidelines and the protocols derived from organized screening programs now form the basis of standardized management. This article provides a detailed review of the radiological criteria, decision-making algorithms, and the role of transthoracic needle biopsy in the management of pulmonary nodules.

title: Endoscopy timing in managing acute esophagogastric variceal bleeding: a multicenter retrospective study.
abstract: Background Patients suffering from acute esophagogastric variceal bleeding (AEGVB) frequently face unfavorable prognoses. Although endoscopy is the preferred intervention for AEGVB, the optimal timing for its administration to enhance patient outcomes remains a subject of ongoing debate. Methods This study encompassed patients with cirrhosis who presented with AEGVB and received endoscopic treatment at three major tertiary hospitals in Shandong Province, China, from January 2017 to July 2024. Participants were stratified based on the time interval from hospital admission to endoscopic intervention (<12 h vs. ≥12 h; <24 h vs. ≥24 h; <48 h vs. ≥48 h; <72 h vs. ≥72 h). Propensity score matching (PSM) was utilized in a 1:1 ratio for each group. Subgroup analyses were performed based on patients' hematemesis status, Child-Pugh classification, and Model for End-Stage Liver Disease (MELD) score. The primary outcomes assessed included overall post-endoscopic rebleeding, 5-day rebleeding, 6-week rebleeding, rebleeding beyond 180 days, in-hospital mortality, and 6-week mortality. Furthermore, a multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression model was employed to identify risk factors for rebleeding. Results Overall, 1125 patients who underwent endoscopic intervention for AEGVB were included. Prior to PSM, the group undergoing endoscopy within 12 h exhibited a significantly higher in-hospital mortality rate compared to the group undergoing endoscopy after 12 h (3.3%vs. 0.5%, P = 0.010). Post-PSM analysis revealed no significant differences between the two groups regarding in-hospital and 6-week mortality, overall post-endoscopic rebleeding, 5-day rebleeding, 6-week rebleeding, and rebleeding occurring beyond 180 days. In a subgroup analysis of patients presenting with hematemesis, those in the <24-hour group demonstrated a significantly higher incidence of overall post-endoscopic rebleeding (50.4%vs. 37.9%, P = 0.015) and rebleeding beyond 180 days post-treatment (29.9%vs. 19.3%, P = 0.014) compared to the ≥24 h group. Additionally, in the subgroup analysis of patients classified as Child-Pugh class B, the <24-hour group showed a significantly elevated rate of overall post-endoscopic rebleeding compared to the ≥24-hour group (50.0%vs. 38.2%, P = 0.026). This rate was also significantly higher in the <72-hour group compared to the ≥72-hour group (44.8%vs. 35.1%, P = 0.018). Notably, the incidence of rebleeding beyond 180 days post-endoscopic therapy was higher in the <72-hour group compared to the ≥72-hour group (25.2%vs. 17.7%, P = 0.029). Multivariate Cox regression analysis indicated that the timing of endoscopic therapy was not an independent risk factor for rebleeding. Conclusions In conclusion, for patients with AEGVB who can tolerate endoscopy, early endoscopic intervention may not enhance the overall prognosis.

title: International consensuses and guidelines on etiology, diagnosis, and treatment of retinal vein occlusion (RVO) by the Academy of Asia-Pacific Professors of Ophthalmology (AAPPO), Asia-Pacific Vitreo-retina Society (APVRS) and Academia Retina Internationalis (ARI).
abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is a prevalent potentially blinding retinal vascular disease, with secondary macular edema, retinal ischemia, and ocular neovascular complications posing substantial threats to visual function. Supported by members of the Academy of Asia-Pacific Professors of Ophthalmology (AAPPO), Asia-Pacific Vitreo-retina Society (APVRS) and Academia Retina Internationalis (ARI), a consensus and guideline is provided a comprehensive update on the etiology, diagnosis and management of RVO. An updated consensus was judged necessary following numerous recent results from epidemiology studies, evolution of advanced imaging technologies and novel pharmacotherapeutics from clinical trials, including an expanding portfolio of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) agents, drug delivery systems, and emerging evidence on relevant artificial intelligence. The formulation of these consensus statements were based on the review and discussion of a systematic search for the latest evidence-based data and voting by an International Panel of Experts (IPE) in the following key areas: I) Diagnostic controversies around classification systems and imaging modalities; II) Treatment controversies regarding anti-VEGF therapy, corticosteroid treatments, laser therapy, and surgical interventions; III) Management paradigm between standardized protocols from clinical trials and individualized approaches and IV) Emerging controversies in novel therapeutics. The primary goal was to furnish ophthalmologists with standardized, yet individualized, management protocols to try to optimize treatment safety and efficacy, ensuring alignment with contemporary clinical practices in the Asia-Pacific region.

title: Barriers to artificial intelligence applications in ophthalmology: beyond diagnostic accuracy toward patient outcomes, workflow integration, ethics, and trust.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a major area of ophthalmic innovation, with a rapidly expanding literature, yet routine clinical adoption remains limited. Diagnostic accuracy alone is an insufficient marker of clinical value because even technically strong systems may fail to improve referral, follow-up, treatment, clinician workload, or health-system value. This focused narrative review examines the barriers that separate ophthalmic AI performance from real-world implementation. We reviewed ophthalmic AI literature indexed in PubMed, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, with emphasis on studies published from January 2018 to September 2026 and on prospective, randomized, real-world, economic, governance, and patient-centred evidence. We organize translation across four linked domains: algorithmic validity, clinical utility, workflow integration, and health-system value, with ethical governance and trust as cross-cutting requirements. Diabetic retinopathy screening now provides a concrete translational example spanning large-scale retrospective validation, prospective deployment, workflow implementation, and economic evaluation. We also consider how foundation models and large language models alter evidence requirements because outputs can depend on prompts, retrieved context, tools, and model versions. For glaucoma, retinal disease management, retinopathy of prematurity, anterior segment applications, and automated reporting, evidence remains less mature. The central challenge for ophthalmic AI is therefore no longer model development alone, but disciplined clinical translation, including prospective evaluation, operational workflow measurement, equity assessment, lifecycle monitoring, transparent governance, and trustworthy implementation.

title: Integrating deep learning and radiomics for accurate differentiation of benign and malignant breast microcalcifications on intraoperative specimen mammography.
abstract: Background Mammography (MG) remains the cornerstone imaging modality for early breast cancer screening, playing a pivotal role in lowering disease-specific mortality. Nevertheless, its diagnostic utility is constrained by a substantial false-negative rate, documented between 10% and 30%. This limitation poses significant clinical challenges in evaluating suspicious microcalcifications on surgical excision biopsy. Intraoperative frozen section analysis often yields inconclusive findings for such calcified lesions, potentially necessitating re-operation. Consequently, rigorous assessment of mammographic features in excised specimens is essential for optimizing surgical decision-making, particularly regarding the necessity and timing of intraoperative pathological evaluation. Methods This investigation involved a retrospective evaluation of 400 intraoperative specimen mammography obtained from individuals confirmed to have breast cancer at the Guangdong Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine. We herein focus exclusively on intraoperative specimen mammography, which is distinct from conventional screening mammography. Upon securing necessary ethical clearance, we assembled a rigorously screened dataset comprising 197 benign and 203 malignant instances. Prior to analysis, images were subjected to preprocessing steps such as grayscale transformation and histogram equalization to optimize them for deep learning ingestion. We subsequently constructed the EfficientNet_radiomics framework by fusing latent representations from the EfficientNet-B0 architecture with manually engineered radiomic descriptors extracted from the imaging data, a strategy designed to augment the system's diagnostic precision. Results Compared with conventional machine learning approaches and experienced radiologists, our framework yielded superior diagnostic metrics. Notably, it achieved 78.0% ± 7.0 accuracy in identifying benign calcifications versus 71.4% ± 8.0 for radiologists, and 83.0% ± 6.0 versus 81.8% ± 6.0 for malignant lesions, underscoring its translational value for clinical deployment. Conclusion The study holds promise as a real-time decision-support tool during intraoperative specimen evaluation, potentially reducing unnecessary frozen section analyses and re-operation rates by providing more accurate intraoperative differentiation, particularly for benign calcifications.

title: Validation of a 3D-printed anthropomorphic eye phantom for quality assurance in external beam radiotherapy using TLD and radiochromic film.
abstract: External beam radiation therapy (EBRT) is widely used for uveal melanoma to preserve the eye and achieve effective tumor control. However, late side effects remain a concern, reinforcing the need for dose reduction to mitigate long-term toxicity. This study aims to validate a 3D-printed ocular tissue-equivalent anthropomorphic phantom, with enhanced anatomical accuracy based on the Alderson Radiation Therapy Phantom, through end-to-end dosimetric analysis using radiochromic film and thermoluminescent dosimeters (TLDs) for research and quality assurance (QA) applications in EBRT. Gafchromic EBT3 films and LiF:Mg,Ti microcube TLDs were used for dose assessment in target volume and organs at risk (OAR). Calibration and irradiation were performed using a Varian Clinac iX and a TrueBeam linear accelerator with a 6 MV photon beam. Film dosimetry, with films positioned in axial and oblique planes, was processed using the Film2Dose software and compared to the Varian Eclipse® treatment planning system (TPS) via gamma analysis. For TLD analysis, lower limit of detection verification, reproducibility tests, individual calibration, and cone beam computed tomography (CBCT) dosimetry were made prior to the treatment dosimetry to ensure accuracy. For treatment dosimetry, TLD samples were placed in regions of interest (i.e. lens, eye fundus, PTV, and optic nerve) for point dose verification and compatibility analysis against the TPS. In the film analysis, maximum dose uncertainties of up to 16% were observed in low-dose regions (<10% of prescribed dose). Gamma analysis yielded a mean passing rate of 100% for 2%/2 mm/10% threshold criterion. All TLDdose measurements demonstrate statistical compatibility with TPS predictions using Z-score-based compatibility analysis. Uncertainties below 5% were found in experimental measurements and TPS point dose assessment. These results indicate the robustness of the dosimetric methods employed and support the validation of the developed 3D-printed, tissue-equivalent anthropomorphic ocular phantom for research and quality assurance applications in EBRT.

title: Enhanced two-stage cascaded network for high-precision stopping power ratio and functional image generation from conventional CT.
abstract: Purpose Accurate stopping power ratio (SPR) estimation is essential for proton therapy dose calculation; however, SPR and related functional images-electron density (ED), effective atomic number (Zeff), and iodine concentration (IC)-currently require dual-energy CT (DECT), whose clinical adoption is limited by high cost and restricted availability. To our knowledge, no previous study has synthesized DECT-derived functional images directly from conventional single-energy CT (SECT). This study proposes, for the first time, a deep learning framework that generates SPR, ED, Zeff, and IC maps simultaneously from conventional CT, and investigates whether a physics-informed two-stage cascaded architecture can outperform conventional single-stage networks. Methods Seventy-four head-and-neck cancer patients scanned with a dual-layer DECT scanner were retrospectively analyzed. Integrated detector-layer signals provided SECT-equivalent input images, while DECT-derived maps served as references. Four networks were compared: a single-output UNet (UNet-1), a multi-output UNet (UNet-4), a two-stage cascaded UNet (Cascade-UNet), and the proposed enhanced two-stage cascaded model (Cascade-New), which incorporates an asymmetric encoder-decoder with residual vision modules and Mamba-based dense connectivity, and exploits the physical dependency chain CT → ED/Zeff → SPR through a three-term training loss. Models were evaluated on an independent test set using mean absolute error (MAE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index measure (SSIM), and Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC), with pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Results The proposed Cascade-New model achieved the best overall performance: the lowest SPR MAE (11.65 ± 1.58 in units of SPR × 10 -3 vs. 12.99 ± 1.46 for UNet-4, a 10.3% relative reduction), the highest SSIM (0.9971 ± 0.0016), and the strongest correlation (PCC = 0.9996 ± 0.0002). Improvements over UNet-4 in ED, Zeff, and IC synthesis were all statistically significant (all p = 0.031). Visual and error map analyses confirmed its improved performance, particularly in bone and heterogeneous tissue regions. Conclusion This study provides the first demonstration that SPR and other DECT-derived functional images can be synthesized directly from conventional SECT with high precision. The proposed physics-informed cascaded framework offers a cost-effective alternative to DECT, enabling radiotherapy centers to obtain accurate SPR maps with conventional CT for proton dose calculation, potentially reducing range uncertainty and expanding access to high-precision functional imaging.

Models were evaluated on an independent test set using mean absolute error (MAE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), structural similarity index measure (SSIM), and Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC), with pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests.

Results

The proposed Cascade-New model achieved the best overall performance: the lowest SPR MAE (11.65 ± 1.58 in units of SPR × 10-3 vs. 12.99 ± 1.46 for UNet-4, a 10.3% relative reduction), the highest SSIM (0.9971 ± 0.0016), and the strongest correlation (PCC = 0.9996 ± 0.0002). Improvements over UNet-4 in ED, Zeff, and IC synthesis were all statistically significant (all p = 0.031). Visual and error map analyses confirmed its improved performance, particularly in bone and heterogeneous tissue regions.

Conclusion

This study provides the first demonstration that SPR and other DECT-derived functional images can be synthesized directly from conventional SECT with high precision. The proposed physics-informed cascaded framework offers a cost-effective alternative to DECT, enabling radiotherapy centers to obtain accurate SPR maps with conventional CT for proton dose calculation, potentially reducing range uncertainty and expanding access to high-precision functional imaging.

title: Progression of White Matter Hyperintensities in Older Adults: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) are ubiquitous on magnetic resonance images (MRI) in older adults. However, the rate and mechanisms of their proliferation remain unclear, as they are inferred mainly from cross-sectional studies and imperfect single indicators of theoretical constructs. To assess the magnitude of WMH change and its modifiers, we conducted a meta-analysis of 54 longitudinal studies. We found the increase in WMH burden over time (pooled effect size) even in the studies with rigorous participant health screening. WMH proliferation was faster in the samples with higher mean age but independent of sample's sex or ethno-racial composition. Higher prevalence of vascular disease in the sample and lower sample average of diastolic or mean arterial pressure at baseline yielded faster mean WMH progression. Lower baseline cognitive status in samples with healthiest participants was associated with faster WMH increase. Automatic and manual methods produced equivalent results, but manual intervention in automatic methods yielded higher estimates. We found no evidence of publication bias. To better quantify the WMH progression and the influence of moderators in future studies, we recommend increasing the number of assessment occasions, applying uniform protocols and instruments, using multiple indicators of risk factors and cognitive outcomes, adding assessment of metabolic, energetic, and hemodynamic properties of the brain, applying state-of-the-art statistical modeling methods, providing comprehensive sample descriptions, and reporting the results in greater detail.

title: Comparing Short-Term Clinical Outcomes and Survivorship of Complex Revision Total Hip Arthroplasty: Custom Triflange Acetabular Implants Vs Standard Cage Reconstruction.
abstract: Background Complex revision total hip arthroplasty poses challenges in cases of severe acetabular bone loss, pelvic discontinuity, or multiple prior revision total hip arthroplasties. This study compares clinical outcomes and implant survivorship between custom triflange acetabular implants (CTAIs) and standard off-the-shelf cup-cage constructs. Methods Between 2016 and 2022, our registry was screened for consecutive patients who received either a CTAI or an off-the-shelf cup-cage construct. A retrospective review assessed patient characteristics, perioperative data, and postoperative outcomes using radiographs and follow-up notes. Primary outcomes were postoperative mortality and reoperation rates. Secondary outcomes included implant migration, bony remodeling, and patient-reported outcomes using Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement (HOOSJR). Kaplan-Meier survival analysis assessed mortality-free survival and implant survivorship. Univariate and multivariate analyses was conducted to determine associations between preoperative variables and postoperative outcomes. Results Among 787 screened patients, 18 met inclusion criteria. Fourteen (78%) had Paprofsky type 3A (28%) or 3B (50%) defects. Eleven (61%) patients received a CTAI, while 7 (39%) received standard off-the-shelf cup-cage constructs. The ΔHOOSJR scores were 37.7 ± 42.4 for off-the-shelf cup-cage constructs and 48.7 ± 30.8 for CTAI, with no significant difference ( P = .531). Two (11%) patients required revision for periprosthetic joint infection, and 4 (22%) expired. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis revealed 75.2% mortality-free survivorship and 78% implant survivorship at 4 years. Conclusions Off-the-shelf cup-cage constructs and CTAIs demonstrated comparable short-term clinical outcomes and implant survivorship in this cohort of patients undergoing complex revision THA. Implant selection may therefore be guided by patient-specific factors and surgeon preference.

title: Reverse Dorr Classification of Lateral Knee Radiographs: A Qualitative Assessment of Bone Quality in Total Knee Arthroplasty.
abstract: Background The Dorr classification is the standard radiographic method for assessing proximal femur bone quality and guiding implant selection in total hip arthroplasty (THA); however, a similar method has not been established for total knee arthroplasty (TKA). Previous studies have demonstrated that radiographic parameters of the distal femur, specifically the ratio of the inner vs outer cortical diameter on lateral knee radiographs, are associated with bone mineral density. The aim of this study was to develop an efficient, reproducible, and qualitative classification system of the distal femur that correlates with bone mineral density to guide implant selection in TKA. Methods A retrospective review of 200 TKA patients with preoperative dual-energy radiograph absorptiometry (DXA) within 1 year of TKA at a single institution was performed. Preoperative lateral knee radiographs were independently reviewed and the degree of anterior cortical taper of the distal femur between the trochlea and a point one patella height (Reverse Dorr 1 [RD1]) or two patella heights (RD2) proximal to the trochlea was graded as Reverse Dorr A, B, or C. Results The Reverse Dorr classification system was associated with DXA T-score, intraoperative physician assessment, and demonstrated moderate to strong interobserver agreement. Reverse Dorr A femurs had a 59-70% predicted probability of normal bone, whereas Reverse Dorr C femurs had a 66-76% predicted probability of osteoporosis. Conclusions The Reverse Dorr classification system is an efficient and reproducible assessment of preoperative bone quality and may serve to inform implant selection in TKA.

title: Integrating the Association Research Circulation Osseous Clinical Practice Guideline into the Diagnosis and Management of Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: Four Illustrative Case Scenarios.
abstract: Background Treatment choices for osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) are based on the patient's age, risk of collapse, lesion size, symptoms, and disease stage. To our knowledge, this represents the first international, evidence-based clinical practice guideline (CPG) developed specifically for the diagnosis and treatment of nontraumatic ONFH, which was recently released by the Association Research Circulation Osseous (ARCO). The CPG offers recommendations that are supported by evidence, but their practical implementation in day-to-day clinical practice may be less intuitive. These case scenarios illustrate the application of the CPG only and do not discuss treatment outcomes, which are discussed in the CPG itself. Methods To illustrate how ARCO CPG recommendations can be applied to a range of ONFH presentations, four relevant clinical cases were chosen. The selection of imaging, evaluation of symptoms, estimation of collapse risk, grounds for observation, use of joint-preserving techniques, and consideration of total hip arthroplasty (THA) are all important diagnostic and therapy choices that are highlighted in each case. Results For small, asymptomatic lesions with little chance of collapse, Case 1 illustrates the value of magnetic resonance imaging in the diagnosis and the suitability of observation. Case 2 shows how core decompression and bone marrow concentrate augmentation can be used to treat symptomatic pre-collapse disease. Case 3 illustrates the decision-making process for a young patient who has bilateral ONFH and needs joint-preserving therapy for the contralateral pre-collapse lesion and THA for one hip with collapse. Case 4 illustrates how patient age, lesion size, and symptom status affect the decision to choose observation over intervention for asymptomatic illness. Conclusion The ARCO CPG provides a practical framework for diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment selection in patients who have ONFH. Application of the guideline recommendations can facilitate evidence-based and patient-centered decision-making across a broad spectrum of clinical scenarios.

title: Elderly-onset rheumatoid arthritis versus polymyalgia rheumatica: A systematic review and meta-analysis on pathophysiology, diagnosis and clinical progression.
abstract: Elderly-onset rheumatoid arthritis (EORA) and polymyalgia rheumatica (PMR) are among the most frequent inflammatory rheumatic diseases in patients over 50, yet their clinical differentiation, particularly when EORA presents with polymyalgic onset, poses a common diagnostic challenge. This systematic review aimed to identify the pathophysiological, clinical, imaging and treatment-response features that distinguish EORA from PMR. MEDLINE, CENTRAL and Scopus (inception to January 2026), with supplementary searches of LILACS, Google Scholar and trial registries (June 2026) were searched, including studies that compared EORA with PMR or reported separately extractable data for both; risk of bias was appraised with design-specific tools and the evidence weighted accordingly. Seventy-one studies across four domains were included: pathophysiology (22 studies), clinical presentation and final diagnosis at follow-up (24 studies), imaging (21 studies), and treatment response (4 studies). Genetically, in one low risk of bias study that stratified EORA by rheumatoid factor status, PMR and seronegative EORA shared HLA-DRB1*13/*14 associations, a pattern distinct from the shared epitope-driven susceptibility of seropositive RA. However, divergent metabolomic signatures suggest different downstream inflammatory mechanisms. An exploratory random-effects meta-analysis yielded a pooled PMR-to-RA reclassification rate of 7% (95% CI 4-12%; 9 studies), narrowing to 4% (95% CI 2-7%) in methodologically robust studies, though rates of reclassification to RA were considerably higher (up to 20%) when patients with undifferentiated polymyalgic presentations were included. Peripheral arthritis occurred in 28% of PMR patients (95% CI 20-35%; 6 studies), with a significant difference between baseline prevalence (21%) and cumulative incidence over follow-up (34%) on subgroup meta-analysis (p = 0.026), and was characteristically transient and glucocorticoid-responsive, whereas persistent synovitis involving wrists and small joints was associated with reclassification to RA. On imaging, evidence from low-to-moderate risk of bias, ultrasound studies showed that shoulder findings overlapped substantially between conditions, whereas bilateral hip synovitis was significantly more frequent in PMR (47% vs 0% in RA), suggesting the hip as a stronger proximal informative site. However, distal joint synovitis demonstrated the highest discriminatory value, with the presence of at least one among RF positivity, hand grey-scale ≥2, or hand power Doppler ≥1 achieving 89% sensitivity and 93% specificity for EORA identification. This review highlights that the distinction between EORA and PMR cannot be reliably established at a single time point and that longitudinal reassessment integrating clinical, serological, and imaging findings remains essential for the differential diagnosis. However, the evidence is limited by clinical and methodological heterogeneity and the predominance of observational designs.

title: Decoding the Aneurysm Thrombus: Radiomic Signatures of Sac Shrinkage After EVAR.
abstract: Aneurysm sac shrinkage after endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) is a surrogate marker of effective aneurysm exclusion and favorable outcomes. Radiomics enables quantitative imaging analysis beyond visual assessment and is increasingly applied in cardiovascular imaging. Analysis of intraluminal thrombusmay may provide additional information for identifying patients with different patterns of sac remodeling after EVAR. This single-center retrospective study assessed whether radiomic features of the intraluminal thrombus extracted from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA), alone and in combination with clinical and anatomical variables, were associated with aneurysm sac shrinkage after EVAR. Patients undergoing elective EVAR for infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm were included and stratified according to sac shrinkage at 12-month follow-up. Preoperative arterial-phase CTA scans were analyzed. The aneurysm sac was manually segmented using 3D Slicer, and the intraluminal thrombus was selected as the region of interest. A total of 530 radiomic features were extracted using PyRadiomics with Laplacian of Gaussian filtering. Features were standardized and evaluated using the Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney test, Pearson correlation filtering, and Akaike Information Criterion-based feature selection. Predictive performance was compared among combined clinical-radiomic, radiomic-only, and clinical-only models. Among 94 patients, 29 showed aneurysm sac shrinkage. Two radiomic features were significantly associated with shrinkage. Younger age (p=0.02), larger aneurysm diameter (p=0.02), and homogeneous thrombus texture were associated with shrinkage, while the absence of COPD was associated with lack of shrinkage. None of the other evaluated clinical or anatomical variables showed a significant association with sac shrinkage. The combined clinical-radiomic model achieved the best performance (AUC 0.76, sensitivity 0.70, specificity 0.75, accuracy 0.73). Preoperative thrombus radiomic features were associated with subsequent sac shrinkage and provided complementary information when integrated with clinical variables. These findings support the potential role of thrombus radiomics in the characterization of sac remodeling after EVAR and warrant validation in larger cohorts.

title: Histological Differentiation of Neovascularisation and Residual Veins in Groin Recurrence.
abstract: Objectives Recurrence in the inguinal region following surgery for saphenofemoral insufficiency remains a major challenge in venous surgery. Histologically, a distinction can be made between residual stump and neovascularization. Using hematoxylin-eosin and Elastica-van Gieson staining, this study systematically analyses samples from recurrent saphenofemoral lesions. Methods Patient demographic data, the clinical CEAP stage, and the Venous Clinical Severity Score were recorded. A preoperative duplex ultrasound was performed. The resected specimens were processed using standard staining methods. During histological examination, a distinction was made between residual venous tissue and neovascularisation. Results A total of 203 samples were available for histopathological evaluation. In the histological evaluation, 197 samples were classified as stump tissue (97.0%) and 6 samples as neovascularization (3.0%). The diagnostic specificity and predictive value of duplex sonography and intraoperative macroscopic classification between residual stump and neovascularisation was limited. Conclusion Residual venous structures represent the predominant morphological substrate of groin recurrences after saphenofemoral surgery. True neovascularisation occurs only in a few cases and should be regarded as a secondary phenomenon rather than a primary cause of recurrence. Surgical precision during the initial intervention may play an important role in recurrence prevention.

title: Laparoscopic Left Renal Vein Transposition for Nutcracker Syndrome: A Single-Center Case Series.
abstract: Background Nutcracker syndrome is a rare vascular compression disorder caused by entrapment of the left renal vein, most commonly between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery. Surgical treatment is reserved for patients with persistent and debilitating symptoms; however, evidence regarding minimally invasive approaches remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of laparoscopic left renal vein transposition in patients with symptomatic nutcracker syndrome. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted of nine consecutive patients who underwent laparoscopic left renal vein transposition for symptomatic nutcracker syndrome between 2019 and 2024 at a single tertiary vascular center. Diagnosis was established using contrast-enhanced computed tomography demonstrating significant left renal vein compression. Perioperative outcomes, complications, length of hospital stay, and clinical symptom resolution during follow-up were assessed. Results The study group included seven women (77.8%) and two men (22.2%), aged 20-52 years. The most common presenting symptom was left flank or lumbar pain. All procedures were completed laparoscopically without conversion to open surgery. Operative time ranged from 180 to 375 minutes, with a median hospital stay of 4 days. One patient experienced major perioperative bleeding requiring transfusion and pleural drainage (Clavien-Dindo IIIb). Most patients achieved complete or substantial symptom relief during follow-up. One patient developed late anastomotic occlusion with symptom recurrence requiring reoperation and venous bypass reconstruction. Conclusions Laparoscopic left renal vein transposition appears to be a safe and effective treatment option for selected patients with symptomatic nutcracker syndrome. The minimally invasive approach provides favorable clinical outcomes with acceptable perioperative morbidity; however, long-term follow-up remains essential because of the risk of anastomotic occlusion and symptom recurrence. Further multicenter studies with larger patient cohorts are required to better define optimal treatment strategies.

title: The type of portal vein reconstruction does not affect the outcomes of pancreatic surgery or the patency of the portal vein.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the safety of the four types of portal vein reconstruction (PVR) as defined by the International Study Group of Pancreatic Surgery (ISGPS) and to analyse long-term survival outcomes in patients with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Methods A prospectively collected pancreatic surgery registry that was supplemented retrospectively was used. Patients who underwent open pancreatic resection with PVR between 2005 and 2024 were included. Clinicopathological characteristics, outcomes, and computed tomography images were analysed and tested in multivariate and survival analyses. For survival analyses, patients with PDAC who underwent pancreatectomy without PVR served as controls. Results Pancreatectomies with PVR (n=386) comprised 63 tangential resections with venorrhaphy (ISGPS type I), 25 patch reconstructions (type II), 147 end-to-end anastomoses (type III), and 151 resections with graft interposition (type IV). Most type IV reconstructions (98.7%) used spiral grafts, predominantly made from the great saphenous vein (GSV). PVR thrombosis rate was 3.1% at 30 days and 5.7% at 90 days following surgery. There were no significant differences between PVR types I-IV in the incidence of PVR thromboses, complications, or mortality. Median survival for PDAC patients with PVR was 22.8 months, with no survival differences between types I-IV, compared with 31.7 months in patients without PVR, p=.003. Conclusions In this setting, where PVR was performed using GSV spiral grafts for interposition, the type of PVR did not associate with pancreatic surgery outcomes or portal vein patency. The rate of PVR thrombosis was low, and other complication rates and long-term survival outcomes were comparable with international standards.

title: Choroid plexus enlargement in Post-COVID-19 syndrome is linked to Serum-Induced cytokine secretion in human hippocampal progenitors.
abstract: Background Post-COVID-19 syndrome (PCS) is characterised by persistent cognitive, affective, and somatic symptoms that extend months beyond acute SARS-CoV-2 infection, frequently in the absence of overt systemic inflammation. While immune dysregulation is increasingly implicated, the mechanisms linking peripheral immune alterations to enduring brain-related symptoms remain poorly understood. The choroid plexus (CP), a specialised blood-cerebrospinal fluid barrier and neuroimmune interface, is well positioned to mediate such immune-brain communication. Methods In this pilot case-control study, we combined high-resolution structural MRI with peripheral immunophenotyping and a functional human neural progenitor model to investigate the neuroimmune relevance of CP morphology in PCS. Twenty individuals with PCS following mild acute COVID-19 and twenty recovered controls underwent MRI for manual CP segmentation, serum cytokine profiling, and serum exposure assays using human hippocampal progenitor cells. Results Individuals with PCS exhibited significantly enlarged CP volume compared with recovered controls, independent of intracranial volume. CP enlargement showed minimal association with circulating cytokine concentrations, indicating limited correspondence with contemporaneous peripheral inflammatory markers. In contrast, CP volume was tentatively associated with serum-induced immune and astrocytic responses in vitro, including reduced IL-8 sretion and altered astrocytic marker expression (GFAP and AQP4), while no associations were observed with neuronal differentiation markers. Conclusions These findings highlight a dissociation between static peripheral cytokine levels and functional brain-relevant immune effects, and suggest that CP enlargement preferentially indexes brain-proximal neuroimmune signalling capacity rather than peripheral inflammatory load alone. By integrating neuroimaging with human cellular assays, this study positions the choroid plexus as a structural marker of persistent neuroimmune dysregulation in PCS and highlights immune-barrier interfaces as critical targets for understanding post-infectious brain symptoms.

title: Artificial intelligence in osteoarthritis and osteoporosis: implications for management and research.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly influencing clinical care and research in osteoarthritis and osteoporosis. For patients, AI can broaden access to health information, including understanding of disease and treatment options. For clinicians, AI-based systems may assist risk stratification and decision-making, including identifying individuals most likely to benefit from specific therapies. In medical imaging, AI approaches can grade osteoarthritis severity, identify occult pathology (including atypical femoral fractures), and estimate low bone mineral density from non-dedicated examinations. In research, AI can facilitate analysis of complex, high-dimensional datasets (e.g., multi-omics and cell-cell communication) supporting the discovery of biomarkers, candidate therapeutic targets and disease endotypes. Emerging directions include agentic AI systems for end-to-end workflows, adaptation of foundation models pre-trained on large, diverse datasets, and carefully evaluated synthetic data for augmentation and validation/quality-control pipelines. This review examines current and emerging AI applications across osteoarthritis and osteoporosis, and pathways for safe, equitable and effective deployment.

title: Microenvironmental barriers to healing in osteoradionecrosis and opportunities for regenerative intervention.
abstract: Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is a debilitating sequela of radiotherapy (RT) for head and neck cancer (HNC), characterized by persistent bone exposure or radiographic non-viability and profound tissue repair failure. Despite advances in radiation delivery and clinical management, ORN remains challenging to treat, with therapeutic strategies largely focused on symptom control, infection mitigation, or surgical reconstruction rather than restoration of regenerative capacity. Emerging evidence suggests that radiation-induced cellular senescence represents a central and underrecognized driver of ORN pathophysiology. Ionizing radiation disrupts the bone microenvironment through sustained vascular injury, impaired osteogenic-angiogenic coupling, chronic inflammation, and the accumulation of senescent bone-resident and stromal cells that secrete a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Together, these changes create a hostile niche that suppresses bone remodeling and wound healing long after radiation exposure. This review synthesizes current understanding of radiation-induced injury to the bone microenvironment, critically evaluates existing classification systems and treatment strategies for ORN, and examines emerging regenerative approaches. We further propose senotherapeutic strategies targeting radiation-induced cellular senescence as a complementary and potentially transformative avenue to restore tissue repair capacity. By integrating regenerative biomaterials with targeted modulation of senescence, future therapies may move beyond palliation toward true biological resolution of ORN. Biomaterial delivery systems (e.g., injectable hydrogels, mineral composite scaffolds, and cryogel platforms) are emerging as promising vehicles for spatiotemporally controlled senotherapeutic delivery within the irradiated bone niche.

title: From passive fillers to active implants: A 3D-printed trilayer piezoelectric scaffold recapitulating native bone hierarchy.
abstract: Critical-sized alveolar bone defects affect over 10 million patients annually, yet current synthetic bone substitutes act as passive osteoconductive fillers with unpredictable outcomes. Native bone, by contrast, achieves robust regeneration through a trilayered hierarchy of cancellous, cortical, and metabolically active periosteal tissues, with intrinsic piezoelectricity converting mechanical loading into endogenous electrical cues. While piezoelectric biomaterials have emerged as promising active implants, existing homogeneous scaffolds fail to recapitulate native bone's structural complexity and electromechanical coupling; to date, no work has combined this trilayer architecture with piezoelectric functionality in a single construct. Here we report a trilayer bioinspired piezoelectric scaffold fabricated via a two-step conformal 3D printing strategy, composed of a strontium-doped β-tricalcium phosphate (Sr-β-TCP) triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) cancellous layer, a dense cortical layer, and a barium titanate/silk fibroin (BTO/SF) piezoelectric periosteal layer. Under non-invasive low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) stimulation, the scaffold generates bioelectrical signals that support robust osteogenic activity and pro-angiogenic potential in vitro . Transcriptomic profiling reveals that these electrical cues are associated with intracellular calcium influx and upregulation of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) and Wnt/β-catenin pathways, consistent with enhanced osteogenic differentiation. In a critical-sized bone defect model, the trilayer scaffold with LIPUS achieves substantially superior bone regeneration relative to controls. This work pioneers the integration of native bone hierarchy with piezoelectric functionality into a single active construct, shifting bone tissue engineering from passive filling to bioelectric-guided repair. Coupling structural biomimicry with electroactive stimulation, this strategy holds potential for future bone regenerative applications, including alveolar bone reconstruction.

title: Oral squamous cell carcinoma: A modern review of pathogenesis and treatment.
abstract: Oral cancer (OC), predominantly oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), is a serious global health burden with high mortality rates, especially in South and Southeast Asia. OC is a severe worldwide health issue that is mostly caused by a sedentary lifestyle, alcohol, tobacco, and areca nut intake. The highest prevalence of OSCC is in India and Southeast Asia. Complex genomic and epigenetic changes, such as TP53 dysfunction, enhanced EGFR alteration, and dysregulation of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathways, in conjunction with tumor-promoting alterations in the tumor microenvironment, contribute to oral carcinogenesis ( Tan et al., 2023). Oral submucous fibrosis (a chronic condition that causes precancerous progression in mouth), and leukoplakia (white or gray patches to form on mucus membrane) are instances of oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs), which are key indicators of cancer conversion. Even with advances in histopathology and imaging, delayed diagnosis remains a major limitation. Salivary biomarkers, liquid biopsy devices, and artificial intelligence-based screening tools are examples of novel diagnostic methods with potential for early diagnosis. Therapeutically, novel approaches such as immunotherapy, targeted therapy, nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems, electro spun nanofibers, and plant-derived phytoformulations offer innovative, multi-targeted strategies with enhanced efficacy and reduce toxicity. However, surgery, radiation, and chemotherapy continue to be the primary treatment approaches. Improving new interventions for OC treatment needs a multifaceted approach that integrates early detection strategies, advanced therapeutic strategies, the use of plant-derived therapeutics, nanotechnology, artificial intelligence, and public health awareness to get better therapeutic outcomes.

title: Radiosynthesis and preliminary evaluation of [ 11 C] and [ 18 F] labelled lacosamide scaffolds for brain PET imaging.
abstract: This study summarizes the automated, transition-metal-free radiosynthesis approach for producing [ 11 C]LCM and its bioisosteric analogue [ 18 F]FLCM, along with preliminary pharmacological and preclinical evaluations of these radiotracers can act as potent brain imaging radiotracer candidates. Radiosynthesis was carried out using an automated synthesis module targeting the terminal 3-oxy site of lacosamide. Physicochemical properties, including hydrophilic behavior and plasma-protein binding profile, were evaluated. Translational validation was performed via in vivo PET/CT imaging and ex vivo biodistribution in healthy Wistar rats. The synthesis module yielded a radiotracer with high radiochemical yield and radiochemical purity. Specific activity was determined to be ~21 .7GBq/μmol for [ 11 C]LCM and ~6.76 GBq/μmole for [ 18 F]FLCM. Both radiotracers show favorable hydrophilic and low PPB profiles. In vivo PET scan and ex vivo study confirmed the brain uptake, renal and hepatic clearance, and minimal off-target uptake. The favorable pharmaceutical profiles establish a promising baseline, further rigorous in vitro receptor-affinity assays and dynamic brain imaging in an animal model are required to validate the translational diagnostic utility of these radiotracers.

title: Mechanism‑targeted therapies for vestibular schwannoma: Emerging molecular pathways and translational horizons.
abstract: Vestibular schwannoma represents a significant clinical challenge characterized by hearing loss, vestibular dysfunction, and cranial nerve morbidity. Despite advancements in surgery and radiotherapy, pharmacological options for recurrent, bilateral, or progressive disease remain limited. This review synthesizes current evidence on the molecular landscape of vestibular schwannoma, focusing on NF2 and Merlin inactivation as the upstream driver. We highlight how Merlin loss dysregulates interconnected signaling networks, specifically ErbB, PI3K Akt mTOR, MAPK, Hippo YAP TAZ, Wnt beta catenin, and NF kappaB. Furthermore, we examine how the tumor microenvironment, including tumor-associated macrophages, cancer associated fibroblasts, angiogenic mediators, and immune checkpoints, facilitates therapeutic resistance and immune evasion. The manuscript discusses the translational potential of diverse targeted inhibitors, including ErbB agents, mTOR inhibitors, and novel RNA based therapies such as circ 0001665. While bevacizumab remains the most clinically validated strategy for NF2related schwannomatosis (NF2-SWN), clinical responses are heterogeneous and durable efficacy is often elusive. We identify critical translational gaps, including the lack of predictive biomarkers and the limitations of current preclinical models in capturing the tumor microenvironment and tumor-induced hearing loss. Finally, we propose a precision medicine framework necessitating biomarker guided patient stratification, rational combination therapies targeting both intrinsic signaling and the microenvironment, and clinical trials that prioritize functional outcomes such as hearing preservation over radiographic response alone. This review provides a conceptual roadmap for transitioning toward mechanism guided treatment of vestibular schwannoma.

title: Anchoring nanozymes on microneedles via nanotemplate sacrificial synthesis for glutathione detection.
abstract: Region-specific dysregulation of glutathione (GSH) reflects neuropsychiatric disorders and tumor progression. Microscale precision sampling combined with timely monitoring of GSH provides region-specific molecular information that may aid in disease diagnosis. To enable minimally invasive brain-compatible intraoperative detection of GSH within a limited surgical time window, we designed a 5 mm × 5 mm on-surface microneedle nanozyme sensing platform by adopting a seed-mediated sacrificial template method. The peroxidase (POD)-like nanozyme Prussian blue (PB) probe was grown in situ on a sacrificial ZIF-67 nanotemplate, which was first anchored to the microneedle surface via in situ nucleation to prevent probe detachment in tissue. The dense PB coating substantially increases the immobilization efficiency of GSH aptamers, enabling selective in situ sampling and accumulation of GSH on the nanozyme. This creates a redox antagonistic effect between PB and GSH, which enables the platform to exhibit high selectivity toward GSH over common redox-active interferents. The quantitative concentration range of 271.3-900 μM (R 2 > 0.99) for GSH is demonstrated in a simulated gelatinous tissue, and GSH levels in brain interstitial fluid could be distinguished within 20 min. Less biopsy tissue and shorter analysis time may help minimize tissue damage and could provide timely intraoperative molecular information, potentially complementing histopathology.

The quantitative concentration range of 271.3-900 μM (R<sup>2</sup> > 0.99) for GSH is demonstrated in a simulated gelatinous tissue, and GSH levels in brain interstitial fluid could be distinguished within 20 min. Less biopsy tissue and shorter analysis time may help minimize tissue damage and could provide timely intraoperative molecular information, potentially complementing histopathology.

title: Orbitocranial resection for treatment of lacrimal gland malignant tumors with intracranial extension.
abstract: Objectives This study reports our experience with multidisciplinary surgical management of lacrimal gland malignant tumors with intracranial extension using the orbitocranial approach. Methods We reviewed treatment strategies and surgical approaches for lacrimal gland malignant tumors with intracranial extension and present 2 illustrative patients who underwent orbitocranial resection at our institution in 2015. Clinical records, radiographic images, histologic sections, and archived pathology specimens were reviewed. Results Both patients underwent orbitocranial tumor resection, followed by postoperative chemoradiotherapy. Orbital reconstruction was performed using a temporalis fascia flap and split calvarial bone grafts, with split-thickness skin grafting to line the orbital cavity. The follow-up periods were 69- and 66-months, respectively. Both patients remained alive without evidence of disease recurrence during follow-up. Conclusions The orbitocranial approach, combined with postoperative chemoradiotherapy, may provide satisfactory local and regional control in selected patients with lacrimal gland malignant tumors with intracranial extension. Long-term surveillance remains important because patients may remain at risk for disease recurrence or distant metastasis.

title: Ultrasound technologies to assess bone health: Past, present and future.
abstract: Background Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) is currently the clinical reference standard for osteoporosis diagnosis and fracture risk assessment. However, it provides only a partial description of bone strength and has practical limitations related to accessibility and ionizing radiation. Over the past three decades, quantitative ultrasound (QUS) technologies have evolved from empirical heel-based measurements to advanced imaging approaches capable of characterizing cortical bone structure and material properties. Objectives To review the development of bone ultrasound technologies, summarize their clinical evidence for fracture risk assessment, and discuss the opportunities and challenges of emerging ultrasound-based approaches. Findings First-generation calcaneal QUS devices demonstrate fracture prediction comparable to peripheral DXA in large prospective studies and remain valuable for fracture risk assessment, particularly where DXA is unavailable or repeated X-ray examinations are undesirable. Their broader clinical adoption was limited mainly by device-specific algorithms, lack of standardization, and the absence of universally accepted diagnostic thresholds. Newer ultrasound technologies extend assessment to clinically relevant skeletal sites, including the hip and spine, or directly quantify cortical bone structure and material properties at peripheral sites. Radiofrequency echographic multi-spectrometry (REMS) has shown encouraging results in cross-sectional and prospective studies but relies on proprietary reference models and algorithms that require greater transparency and independent validation. Second-generation technologies, including cortical backscatter analysis (CortBS) and refraction-corrected imaging, provide quantitative measurements of cortical thickness, porosity-related microstructure, wave speed, attenuation and other biomechanical biomarkers in physical SI units, enabling independent validation and multiparametric fracture-risk modeling. However, until now these technologies have only been validated ex-vivo on human cadaver bones and in-vivo in small exploratory cross-sectional fracture discrimination studies. Multicenter cross-sectional and prospective studies are underway to create reference data and to establish their value for fracture risk prediction. Conclusions Bone ultrasound has progressed from an empirical screening tool to a family of quantitative technologies capable of assessing complementary aspects of bone quality and quantity. Calcaneal QUS is currently the only technology with an established guideline-recognized role in fracture risk assessment. Prospective multicenter fracture risk prediction studies, as well as technical standardization and transparent validation studies showing cross-vendor reproducibility and independent replication are now required to define the clinical role of newer ultrasound technologies and support their integration into future osteoporosis management and clinical routine use.

title: Quantification of bone loss, periosteal bone formation and novel histopathological changes in a mouse implant-related Staphylococcus aureus infection model.
abstract: Implant-associated bone infection involves a complex interplay between pathogenic stimuli and host cell responses, yet analysis in preclinical models has typically relied on qualitative or semi-quantitative measures. We aimed to establish a quantified evaluation framework to define host-pathogen relationships in a preclinical implant infection model. Staphylococcus aureus-coated stainless-steel implants were inserted trans-cortically in mouse tibiae and bone changes recorded longitudinally by in vivo micro-CT. An automated segmentation task list was developed to independently isolate and quantify cortical, periosteal-reactive, and trabecular bone compartments. RGB trichrome histomorphometry was used to quantify bone matrix integrity, osteocyte lacunar geometry, and osteoclastic activity. Droplet digital PCR was used to determine absolute bacterial and host genome copy number. Infected implants produced marked reductions in trabecular bone volume fraction, number, and bone mineral density (BMD), together with decreased cortical bone volume fraction and increased cortical porosity, accompanied by significant elevations in periosteal bone volume fraction. Histologically, infected bone exhibited increased eroded surface indicative of osteoclastic resorption, extensive degraded bone matrix and pathological remodelling of osteocyte lacunae toward circularity, consistent with an osteocytic osteolysis response. Infection-induced changes to cortical bone structure correlated mostly with host cell rather than bacterial load; however, cortical BMD negatively correlated with the bacterial:host genome ratio. This multifaceted, quantified framework reveals distinct pathobiological effects of implant-associated infection on trabecular, cortical, and periosteal bone compartments, bone matrix and osteocyte and osteoclast populations, consistent with reports in human patients, suggesting that major pathological changes are driven by the host bone cell response to infection.

title: Clinical phenotype and bone microarchitecture of cutaneous-skeletal hypophosphatemia syndrome: experience from a single center in China.
abstract: Context Cutaneous-skeletal hypophosphatemia syndrome (CSHS) is a rare mosaic RASopathy characterized by epidermal or melanocytic nevi, skeletal dysplasia, and fibroblast growth factor 23 (FGF23)-mediated hypophosphatemic rickets. However, its bone microarchitectural features remain underdefined. Objectives The study aimed to characterize the clinical, genetic, and skeletal microarchitectural features of CSHS. Methods We summarized clinical findings of 6 CSHS patients with genetically confirmed somatic RAS mutations. Skeletal involvement was assessed by whole-body bone scintigraphy. High-resolution peripheral quantitative computed tomography parameters at the distal radius and tibia were compared with age- and sex-matched XLH controls (1:3). Literature review of 24 genetically confirmed CSHS patients was performed to assess genotype-phenotype correlation. Results All patients were confirmed to carry somatic HRAS or NRAS mutation in affected skin. Hypophosphatemia, elevated alkaline phosphatase and elevated FGF23 were found in all patients. Genotype-phenotype correlation analysis did not identify any significant biochemical or systemic burden differences across 3 genotypes. Compared with XLH controls, CSHS patients exhibited significantly reduced total and trabecular volumetric BMD (vBMD), with relatively preserved cortical vBMD. Bone cross-sectional geometry was less expanded than in XLH at the tibia. In addition, thinner trabeculae with greater separation were found at the radius, and the distal tibia showed thinner cortices and decreased cortical porosity. Estimated bone stiffness and failure load were significantly lower at both the radius and tibia. Conclusions CSHS is associated with pronounced trabecular vBMD impairment and reduced bone strength compared with XLH controls. These findings are consistent with a combined contribution of intrinsic skeletal dysplasia and chronic hypophosphatemia on bone, although further studies are needed to elucidate these mechanisms.

title: Preliminary study on early microvascular ingrowth into distracted callus during distraction osteogenesis-A non-invasive approach to explore the early growth patterns and possible mechanism of distraction osteogenesis in vivo.
abstract: Background Distraction osteogenesis (DO) is critical for repairing large segmental bone defects. Early callus vascularization is essential for bone regeneration; however, real-time microcirculatory assessment remains lacking. This study aimed to elucidate spatiotemporal microvascular network construction in distracted callus using super-resolution contrast-enhanced ultrasound (SR CEUS) and high-frame-rate contrast-enhanced ultrasound (HiFR CEUS) in a sheep tibial DO model. Methods Six sheep underwent tibial DO. On day 7 of distraction, B-mode ultrasound, "Firefly" imaging, SR CEUS, and HiFR CEUS were performed. Quantitative parameters including vessel density (VD), perfusion index (PI), mean intensity, and peak intensity (PKI) were compared among three regions: central high-perfusion area (CHPA), annular low-perfusion area (ALPA), and peripheral high-perfusion area (PHPA). Results B-mode ultrasound revealed outward bulging of distracted callus. "Firefly" imaging detected microcalcifications. title: Immediate high-dose-rate brachytherapy with volumetric planning for keloids: Clinical outcomes.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate clinical outcomes and toxicity of a standardized protocol of immediate (<6 h postoperative) high-dose-rate (HDR) brachytherapy with volumetric planning in patients with keloids. Methods and materials We conducted a retrospective cohort study including consecutive patients with histologically confirmed keloids treated with surgical excision followed by immediate (<6 h) HDR brachytherapy between April 2014 and November 2025. Treatment was delivered using a uniform fractionation scheme of 12 Gy in three fractions. CT-based planning was performed in all cases, and the clinical target volume (CTV) was defined over the surgical bed. Dosimetric analysis included D90 as the primary coverage parameter. The primary endpoint was local control (LC), defined as recurrence-free interval. Secondary endpoints included late toxicity (RTOG/EORTC) and patient-reported outcomes assessed using the POSAS 3.0 scale. Results A total of 64 keloids were included. Median follow-up was 37.5 months. The overall local control rate was 92.2%, with five recurrences (7.8%), all occurring within the first 24 months. Median D90 was 98.5%. Larger lesions (>5 cm) showed a higher recurrence rate compared to smaller lesions (12.5% vs. 7.1%). No acute toxicity was observed. Late toxicity was limited to mild hypopigmentation (9.4%), grade one telangiectasia (6.3%), and superficial atrophy (4.7%). One case of mild chondritis (1.5%) was reported. Patient-reported outcomes demonstrated minimal residual symptoms and favorable aesthetic and functional outcomes, as reflected by the patient-reported POSAS scores CONCLUSIONS: Immediate (<6 h) HDR brachytherapy with volumetric planning provides high local control and favorable toxicity in keloid treatment. A regimen of 12 Gy in three fractions is feasible and well-tolerated, representing a valid option in the multidisciplinary management of keloids.

title: Deep learning-assisted needle artifact suppression for enhanced anatomical visualization in prostate high-dose-rate brachytherapy ultrasound imaging.
abstract: Purpose Implanted needles introduce acoustic artifacts that degrade transrectal ultrasound (TRUS) images during high-dose-rate (HDR) prostate brachytherapy, complicating ultrasound-only contouring. We developed an artificial intelligence (AI) needle eraser to remove needles and associated artifacts and facilitate structure delineation. Methods TRUS images from 120 patients undergoing HDR prostate brachytherapy were retrospectively collected. Three-dimensional volumes were acquired immediately before and after needle insertion. A Cycle Generative Adversarial Network (CycleGAN) was trained to transform postneedle images into needle-free images. Two physicians independently rated clinical utility for prostate and urethra delineation using a four-point scale (1 = poor; 4 = excellent). Prostate and urethra contours from preneedle and needle-erased images were compared with clinical reference contours using Dice similarity coefficient (DSC). Results The AI tool suppressed needles and associated artifacts, improving visualization of the prostate and urethral lumen. Mean reader scores were 3.80 ± 0.43 for prostate and 3.75 ± 0.37 for urethra delineation. Compared with preneedle contours, needle-erased contours showed higher agreement with clinical references: prostate DSC increased from 0.91 to 0.93, and urethra DSC increased from 0.70 to 0.89. Conclusions A CycleGAN-based needle eraser can generate needle-free ultrasound images from postinsertion scans and improve visualization and contour agreement for physician delineation.

title: Early postnatal brain volumes and two-year cognitive outcomes in preterm infants: An exploratory machine learning study.
abstract: Introduction Premature birth is associated with an increased risk of cognitive and motor developmental problems. Early prediction of these outcomes is crucial for timely intervention and adequate follow-up. This study aimed to predict cognitive and motor outcomes in preterm-born infants using brain volumetric features in combination with clinical and demographic perinatal characteristics, and to compare the performance of three different machine learning algorithms. Methods We acquired quantitative structural brain MRI at approximately 30 weeks postmenstrual age (PMA) and clinical and demographic birth characteristics including gestational age, sex, birthweight, and maternal education level. Machine learning techniques were applied to predict cognitive (N = 63) and motor (N = 41) outcomes at two years corrected age, assessed using the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development III, in infants born before 30 weeks gestation. We evaluated the performance of logistic regression, linear support vector classifier (linear SVC), and k-nearest neighbour (KNN). Results Employing volumetric features only, KNN achieved a validation accuracy of 0.64, showing modest predictive power for cognitive outcomes. Adding clinical characteristics did not significantly improve accuracy. The models did not perform better than chance when predicting motor outcomes. Conclusion Volumetric features demonstrated modest predictive ability for cognitive outcomes, and the addition of clinical features did not significantly improve performance. The low to moderate overall validation accuracy underscores, however, the challenges faced in the clinical application of machine learning in neuroimaging. The reliability and clinical applicability of predictions of outcomes from advanced neuroimaging data will largely depend on the quantity and quality of the data, methodological standardisation, and the generalisability of the prediction models.

title: Biomechanical insights into traumatic brain injury in Females: Current understanding and future directions.
abstract: The incidence of traumatic brain injury (TBI) in females has increased in recent decades, driven by socioeconomic changes and greater participation in high-risk activities. This rise, combined with the historically limited availability of experimental data from female subjects, highlights the pressing need to improve both the quantity and quality of sex-specific data. Research has identified systematic differences between males and females in brain volume, tissue stiffness, and gray/white matter composition. While differences in brain size are often linked to body dimensions, sex-specific disparities in biomechanical properties, such as viscoelasticity and regional stiffness, may influence TBI susceptibility. Imaging-based techniques, particularly Magnetic Resonance Elastography (MRE), have revealed that female brains tend to exhibit higher stiffness in regions like the occipital and temporal lobes, suggesting a differential biomechanical response to TBI. These regional differences may also serve as potential biomarkers for the diagnosis, monitoring, and tracking the progression of neurodegenerative diseases such as multiple sclerosis, aiding in the assessment of disease progression and therapeutic response. Despite these insights, most current finite element head models (FEHMs) rely on population-averaged parameters that may not adequately represent female-specific tissue mechanics. This review highlights the need to incorporate sex-specific mechanical properties into numerical simulations to improve the accuracy of TBI risk assessments and injury prediction. We emphasize the need for future studies using imaging, experimental methods, and computational modeling to better understand the biomechanical behavior of female brain tissue. Such efforts are essential for advancing personalized approaches to brain injury prevention, diagnosis, and treatment in females.

title: Single-cell RNA sequencing reveals vascular heterogeneity and cell-cell communication remodeling in the glioma blood-tumor barrier.
abstract: Background The blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts drug delivery in glioma, yet its pathologically remodeled counterpart, the blood-tumor barrier (BTB), is a promising therapeutic target. A comprehensive view of the cellular composition and transcriptional heterogeneity of the vascular compartment across the BBB-to-BTB transition is essential for improving glioma therapy. Methods We performed a secondary single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis of the public GSE242044 dataset (7 patients; 13 tumor and adjacent non-tumor surgical specimens, comprising IDH-mutant lower-grade gliomas and IDH-wild-type gliomas). After stringent quality control, doublet removal, Harmony batch correction, and annotation with SingleR plus canonical markers, we dissected vascular cell heterogeneity and performed differential expression, Gene Set Variation Analysis (GSVA), pseudotime (Monocle/Slingshot), and CellChat ligand-receptor inference, with sample-level statistical comparisons (Kruskal-Wallis and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests on per-specimen values). Findings were assessed in three independent glioma scRNA-seq cohorts (GSE162631, GSE117891, GSE174554) and in the CGGA bulk cohort. Results Vascular cell composition (relative representation among the profiled vascular-enriched cells) showed trends across conditions: endothelial cells declined from 60.6 % to 47.5 %, whereas pericytes (15.8 % to 18.0 %) and immune cells increased in IDH-wild-type tumors (macrophages 1.3 % to 7.0 %; T cells 3.0 % to 7.5 %); astrocytes increased from 1.1 % to 4.5 %; these specimen-level trends were mostly not statistically significant (Supplementary Table S1). Cell-cell communication was predicted to be rewired, shifting from pericyte-smooth muscle cell crosstalk in non-tumor and IDH-mutant tissues toward pericyte-astrocyte and predicted vascular-immune interactions in IDH-wild-type tumors. Differential expression and enrichment analyses identified an IDH-wild-type vascular program dominated by extracellular matrix remodeling (COL1A1, COL3A1, COL4A1, LAMB1, TIMP1) and angiogenic activation (ANGPT2), with loss of quiescent endothelial markers (CA4, KLF2). Candidate markers (COL1A1, COL3A1, F3, S100A4, CSPG4, ANGPT2) showed no consistent prognostic association across independent cohorts. Conclusions This secondary analysis delineates transcriptional heterogeneity of BBB/BTB vascular cells and their inferred communication remodeling in glioma. The identified subtype markers are candidate biomarkers that require independent validation; our findings provide a framework for future studies-including spatial and protein-level validation of the candidate markers, functional permeability and coculture assays of the predicted vascular-immune interactions, and preclinical testing of BTB-modulating delivery strategies such as focused-ultrasound-mediated opening in glioma models.
